sources.title: Didi backend interview note exact balanced-binary-tree prompt
Fresh height-sentinel versus recomputed-height oracle validation

claims.text: The source asks only whether a tree is balanced; formal balance definition, API, empty behavior and AVL/BST ordering are not preserved source constraints.
The candidate explicitly adopts standard height-balance semantics and does not add BST ordering.
Fixed cases and 5000 randomized trees exactly match an independent recomputed-height oracle, including hidden internal imbalance.

5000 deterministic randomized trees match an independent oracle that recomputes child heights

boundary_tests.case: equal root subtree heights with deeper internal imbalance

findings: The repository source asks only to determine whether a tree is a balanced binary tree and does not preserve a formal balance definition, language/API, empty-tree rule, or AVL/BST ordering requirement.
The candidate explicitly adopts the standard height-balanced interpretation and separates it from AVL/BST validity instead of inventing source constraints.
The postorder sentinel invariant combines height computation and failure propagation so each visited node is processed once.
Fresh executable validation covers fixed boundaries and 5000 deterministic randomized trees against an independent oracle that recomputes child heights.
The corpus includes both balanced and unbalanced trees and a case where equal root-side heights mask deeper internal imbalance.
The stated O(n) time and O(h) recursion-space bounds match the implementation, with the O(n^2) repeated-height alternative correctly identified as avoidable.
No fabricated project experience or unrelated generated-baseline content remains.
